sections.h2: Where is Fairfield, Connecticut, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Fairfield is a shoreline town in Fairfield County that borders Bridgeport, Trumbull, Easton, Weston and Westport. The 2020 census counted 61,512 residents, and Wikipedia lists a 2024 estimate of 65,300.

The town covers 31.38 square miles, with 29.9 of them land and 1.48 water, and it sits in the Greater Bridgeport Planning Region. ZIP codes are 06824, 06825 and 06828. Roger Ludlow founded the plantation in 1639.

Fairfield works as a group of sections more than one center. Named areas include Southport, Greenfield Hill, Stratfield, Tunxis Hill, the University area, Grasmere, Mill Plain, Knapp's Village, Melville Village, Holland Hill, Murray and the Fairfield Beach area. Two shopping strips, the Post Road (Route 1) and Black Rock Turnpike, tie them together.

sections.h2: What is the history of Fairfield?
sections.html:
Fairfield's best-known event is the burning of July 7, 1779, when about 2,000 British troops landed near Pine Creek Point and burned the town for its support of independence. George Washington noted the damage still visible when he passed through a decade later.

Several nearby municipalities were carved from Fairfield: Redding in 1767, Weston in 1787, Bridgeport in 1821, Westport in 1835, and Easton from Weston in 1845.

The twentieth century changed the town's character. Munitions work in Bridgeport during World War I pushed residents out to Fairfield, and the population grew from about 6,000 to 17,000 by 1929. The Connecticut Turnpike in the 1950s brought another wave, and by the 1960s the suburban pattern was set. General Electric kept its headquarters in town from about 1970 until it moved to Boston on May 8, 2017.

sections.h2: What does the Fairfield shoreline mean for owning and selling a house?
sections.html:
Fairfield has about 5 miles of Long Island Sound coastline, five lifeguarded town beaches, and several tidal waterways. Houses near water carry questions that inland houses do not.

The rivers and creeks named by Wikipedia are Mill River, Rooster River, Ash Creek, Sasco Brook and the Aspetuck River. Southport Harbor and the town marina at South Benson add boating access. Wikipedia also notes that the Fairfield Beach area has seen many new homes built close to the beach and downtown.

  • Ask whether a house sits in a mapped flood zone before you set a timeline; your lender or insurer can check this.
  • Look at the age of any bulkhead, seawall or septic system on waterfront lots.
  • Expect buyers to ask for elevation and insurance history on low-lying streets.

We do not state a flood rule for Fairfield because we did not open a town page on the topic. The town's building office can tell you what applies to a given address.

sections.h2: Who are the biggest employers and institutions in Fairfield?
sections.html:
Higher education and a few long-established headquarters anchor the local economy. Fairfield enrolls more than 17,000 students between Sacred Heart University and Fairfield University, according to Wikipedia.

sections.h2: How do roads, trains and buses serve Fairfield?
sections.html:
Fairfield is crossed by U.S. 1, Interstate 95 and the Merritt Parkway. It also has three Metro-North Railroad stations: Fairfield-Black Rock, Fairfield and Southport.

Local buses are run by the Greater Bridgeport Transit Authority. How far a house sits from a platform or an I-95 exit is one of the first things a commuter buyer checks.

The public schools are Fairfield Warde and Fairfield Ludlowe high schools, Roger Ludlowe, Tomlinson and Fairfield Woods middle schools, and eleven elementary schools. Catholic options include Fairfield Prep and Notre Dame, and private schools include Fairfield Country Day and Unquowa.

sections.h2: When are Fairfield property taxes due?
sections.html:
Fairfield real estate taxes are due quarterly on July 1, October 1, January 1 and April 1. The Tax Collector's due dates page adds that any bill of $100 or less is due in full with the first installment.

The same page says never to ignore a bill. Taxes stay due and interest keeps building until the bill is paid or the Tax Assessor removes it, and not receiving a bill does not excuse a late payment.

ItemDue
Real estateJuly 1, October 1, January 1, April 1
Motor vehicleJuly 1 each year
Supplemental motor vehicleJanuary 1
Business personal propertyJuly 1 and January 1
Sewer use, bills over $300October 1 and April 1

We did not confirm the current Fairfield mill rate or the interest rate on late bills on an opened page, so ask the Tax Collector.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Fairfield assessment?
sections.html:
You file a petition with the Board of Assessment Appeals, and for the 2026 Grand List it must be received in the Assessor's Office by Friday, February 19, 2027, at 4:30 pm. The Fairfield appeals page says postmarks are not accepted.

Petitions can be emailed to assessor@fairfieldct.org, and each property needs its own petition. Real estate appeals should include a copy of the property card, and a representative needs a notarized affidavit.

  • The Assessor's Office mails a hearing notice on or before March 1, and hearings run through March.
  • Each hearing gets 15 minutes, and testimony is sworn and recorded.
  • Decisions come later at a separate meeting, and the Board can raise an assessment as well as lower it.
  • If you still disagree, you can apply to Superior Court within 60 days of the mailed notice.

For the 2025 Grand List the Board chose not to hear commercial properties assessed over $1,000,000, as state law allows. Owners of those properties file with the court directly.

sections.h2: What happens with Fairfield taxes and the state conveyance tax at a sale?
sections.html:
A Fairfield seller settles the tax bill through closing and also deals with the state's conveyance tax return. The return, Form OP-236, is filed by the grantor or the grantor's attorney or agent when the deed is recorded, and the state treats $2,000 or more of consideration as taxable unless an exemption fits.

Fairfield's code on that form is 051. Certain situations are exempt, including a deed in lieu of foreclosure on a principal residence and a principal residence sold for too little to pay its mortgages and priority tax liens. See the Department of Revenue Services page for the full list.

We left out the rate schedule because we did not open a page that gave it. Your closing agent can calculate the Fairfield figure.

sections.h2: What do Fairfield sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Fairfield sellers tend to deal with older houses on small lots, shoreline questions, and a quarterly tax calendar that can leave one installment open at closing.

  • Houses near the beach can carry deferred maintenance, so sellers often get an inspection first.
  • An inherited house can sit through several quarterly due dates while the estate sorts out ownership.
  • Owners with tenants in place may need to sort out a lease before closing.

A cash purchase can remove the repair list and the waiting. The buyer closes on the house as it stands, and the title company pays any tax that is still open out of the proceeds.

faqs.q: When are Fairfield property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real estate tax is due quarterly on July 1, October 1, January 1 and April 1. Any bill of $100 or less is due in full with the first installment.

faqs.q: What is the Fairfield appeal deadline?
faqs.a: For the 2026 Grand List, petitions must be received by the Assessor's Office by 4:30 pm on Friday, February 19, 2027. Postmarks are not accepted, but email to assessor@fairfieldct.org is allowed.

faqs.q: How long is a Fairfield assessment hearing?
faqs.a: Each hearing is allotted 15 minutes. Testimony is sworn and recorded, and the Board decides later at a separate meeting.

faqs.q: Can the Fairfield Board of Assessment Appeals raise my assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. The town's appeals page says the Board can increase an assessment as well as decrease it, so file only if you have solid evidence.

faqs.q: What is Fairfield's town code for the conveyance tax form?
faqs.a: The code is 051 on Form OP-236, according to the state Department of Revenue Services table.

faqs.q: Do I owe tax if I never got a Fairfield tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The Tax Collector's page says failure to receive a bill does not exempt the taxes or the interest, and you should call the office if a bill does not arrive.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fairfield house that has unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Open tax is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, so a seller can sell the house as-is with the balance still due.
